steps.text: Taking the flag. `--rate-limit` on `harborctl keys set`, so a plan's ceiling can be changed without a dashboard round trip.
Parsed and validated. It refuses a value above the plan's own ceiling rather than silently clamping — a clamp reads as success and isn't.

Either. A bare integer is requests per minute. A plan name — `free`, `team` — takes that plan's ceiling from `quota.ts`, so ops can say `--rate-limit team` without knowing the figure, and it moves when the plan does.
Before I cut it — one choice the flag can't take back after it ships.

questions.question: Which plans may --rate-limit change from the CLI?

options.label: free
options.description: 600 a minute today; ops raise it for trials.

options.label: team
options.description: 6,000 a minute; the plan most tickets are about.

options.label: enterprise
options.description: Contracted ceilings; changing one is a support ticket today.

steps.text: Free and team, then: `--rate-limit` refuses an enterprise key with a pointer to the contract, so a contracted ceiling never moves from a terminal.
Flag's in and documented in `harborctl keys set --help`. Ready for tonight's release.
